question: What is the reader here to do, and which arrangement makes that the obvious thing?
note: A grammar is a set of layout rules, not markup. The agent writes the HTML; the rules say where things may go.

options.use: reference-like content the reader scans: features, plans, schedules, specs
rules: Every section is a 12-column grid: a narrow index column (3 columns) holds the section name or number, the content takes the other 9.
Sections are separated by one full-width rule, never by boxes.
All text is left-aligned; nothing is centred.
Repeated items are rows with a rule between them, not cards.
options.recipe: section: grid grid-cols-12 gap-x-8 border-t border-line; index: col-span-3; content: col-span-9; rows: divide-y divide-line

options.use: one claim with one proof beside it: product page, service, restaurant
rules: Sections are two unequal columns (7/5 or 8/4), and the wide side alternates between text and proof down the page.
The narrow column is never decoration: it holds facts, a list, a figure or a form.
The hero uses the same split; its headline is left-aligned in the wide column.
At most one section in the page breaks the split to run full width.
options.recipe: section: grid grid-cols-12 gap-x-12; wide: col-span-7 or col-span-8; narrow: col-span-5 or col-span-4; alternate with order-*

options.use: a statement: launch, event, portfolio cover, campaign
rules: The first screen is type only: the headline runs the full container width at display size, on at most three lines.
Supporting facts sit in a single row of two to four short columns under a rule, like the small print of a poster.
Each later section opens with one line at h1 size across the width, then its content in columns below.
No more than five sections.
options.recipe: hero: min-h-screen flex flex-col justify-between; headline: text-display max-w-none; small print: grid grid-cols-4 gap-8 border-t border-ink pt-4

options.use: an argument or a story read top to bottom: manifesto, case study, long pricing explanation
rules: One text column of 60 to 70 characters, set on the left third-line of the page (columns 3 to 9), not centred.
Facts, figures and notes hang in the margin column to its right, aligned to the paragraph they belong to.
Images and tables may break out to the full container width; text never does.
Headings are in the same column as the text.
options.recipe: section: grid grid-cols-12 gap-x-8; text: col-start-3 col-span-6 max-w-[68ch]; margin: col-span-3; breakout: col-span-12

options.use: many comparable things: works, dishes, releases, team, cases
rules: The page is a stack of full-width rows; each row is one item: a name at left, two or three facts in fixed columns, an image or figure at right.
Columns keep the same width in every row so facts line up down the page.
Rows are separated by a rule; the hovered or featured row is filled with the surface colour.
The hero is itself the first row, larger.
options.recipe: row: grid grid-cols-12 items-baseline gap-x-8 py-6 border-t border-line; name: col-span-4; facts: col-span-2 each; media: col-span-4

options.use: a product with a few very unequal strengths
rules: One grid of 12 columns and rows of equal height; cells span 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8 columns and one or two rows, and no two neighbouring cells have the same span.
Exactly one cell is dominant (at least 7 columns and 2 rows) and holds the main proof.
Cells differ in content type: a figure, a number, a quote from the brief, a list; never icon plus heading plus line repeated.
At most seven cells.
options.recipe: grid grid-cols-12 auto-rows-[minmax(11rem,auto)] gap-4; dominant: col-span-7 row-span-2; others: col-span-5, col-span-4, col-span-3, col-span-8

options.use: a decision between options: pricing, comparison, plans, specs
rules: The main object of the page is one real table: options as columns, criteria as ruled rows, values in cells, with the recommended column marked by the tint fill.
The hero is short (headline and one sentence) so the table starts in the first screen.
Below the table: the questions a buyer asks, as a two-column list of question and answer, open, not an accordion.
Prices and numbers are right-aligned or centred in their column with tabular figures.
options.recipe: table: w-full border-collapse; th/td: text-left py-4 px-4 border-b border-line; recommended column cells: bg-tint; faq: grid grid-cols-12 with question col-span-4 and answer col-span-8
avoid: three floating price cards with a "Most popular" badge

options.use: a page with distinct chapters for distinct readers
rules: Each section is a full-bleed band with its own fill, cycling ground, surface, ink (with ground-coloured text) and at most one accent or tint band.
Inside a band the layout differs from the band before: columns, then a list, then a single statement, then a table.
Bands meet edge to edge with no gap and no rule.
The ink band holds the one thing the page most wants read.
options.recipe: band: w-full py-24; inner: max-w-7xl mx-auto px-8; dark band: bg-ink text-ground
avoid: the same layout in every band

options.use: working through records: orders, tickets, shipments, invoices
rules: A fixed left rail (about 220 px) with plain text navigation; the current item is marked by a fill, not an icon.
The main area starts with one line: page title at left, the primary action at right.
Below it a row of three or four figures separated by vertical rules (not cards), then one dense table that fills the rest.
Table rows are 40 to 48 px high; status is a word with a small dot, not a coloured pill for every row.
options.recipe: shell: grid grid-cols-[220px_1fr] min-h-screen; figures: grid grid-cols-4 divide-x divide-line border-y border-line; table: w-full text-small

options.use: reading results over time: analytics, finance, usage
rules: No rail: a top bar with the product name, three to five text tabs and the period selector.
The first band is one large figure with its change and a plain chart area drawn with divs or an inline SVG polyline in ink and accent only.
Under it, two unequal columns (8/4): a ruled breakdown table and a short ranked list.
Every number has its unit and its period beside it.
options.recipe: top: flex items-baseline justify-between border-b border-line; body: grid grid-cols-12 gap-x-8; main: col-span-8; side: col-span-4

options.use: triage: inbox, support queue, review, approvals
rules: Three columns: a narrow rail of views, a list of items (about 360 px), and the open item filling the rest.
List rows show sender or title, one line of preview and a time; the open row is filled with surface.
The detail column has a header with the item title and two actions at most, then content at a readable measure.
Nothing floats: no modals, no cards with shadows.
options.recipe: grid grid-cols-[200px_360px_1fr] h-screen; list: divide-y divide-line overflow-hidden; detail: p-8 max-w-[72ch]

options.use: a phone app whose home is a list: tasks, orders, bookings, messages
rules: Each screen is 390 px wide: a large left-aligned title at the top, then full-width rows separated by rules, edge to edge.
A row is at least 56 px high with one primary line, one secondary line and one trailing value or chevron.
The primary action is a single full-width button pinned at the bottom of the screen, above the tab bar when there is one.
No cards inside lists.
options.recipe: screen: w-[390px] min-h-[844px] flex flex-col; rows: divide-y divide-line; row: flex items-center justify-between px-5 py-4 min-h-14
avoid: floating action button plus bottom button

options.use: a phone app about a few rich objects: trips, recipes, accounts, plants
rules: Each screen is 390 px wide with 20 px side padding; objects are large panels stacked vertically, each showing an image or figure and three facts.
The first panel is taller and holds today's or the current object.
A bottom tab bar with three to five text labels; the current tab is marked by a fill or a rule, not colour alone.
One panel style only; panels do not nest.
options.recipe: screen: w-[390px] min-h-[844px] flex flex-col px-5 gap-4; panel: rounded-lg bg-surface p-5; tab bar: mt-auto grid grid-cols-4 border-t border-line

options.use: a phone flow with one decision per screen: checkout, booking, onboarding step, detail view
rules: Each screen is 390 px wide: a back row, a title, the object or the question in the upper half, and the decision controls in a sheet rising from the bottom on the surface colour.
The sheet has a 4 px grab rule, one primary button of full width and at most one secondary text action.
Summary values are a ruled two-column list (label left, value right).
Progress, when shown, is words ("Step 2 of 3"), not dots.
options.recipe: screen: w-[390px] min-h-[844px] flex flex-col; sheet: mt-auto rounded-t-lg bg-surface p-5; summary: divide-y divide-line
